Non-detects arrive with Result Value 0 and are treated as below LOQ.\n#\n# Input: a `dat`-style table (WQX column names). Returns one row per\n# original/replicate pair.\n\nassess_rpd \u003c- function(dat,\n                       original_type  = \"Field Msr/Obs\",\n                       replicate_type = \"Quality Control Field Replicate Msr/Obs\") {\n  stopifnot(requireNamespace(\"dplyr\", quietly = TRUE))\n  key \u003c- c(\"Monitoring Location ID\", \"Activity Start Date\", \"Characteristic Name\",\n           \"Result Sample Fraction\", \"Result Analytical Method ID\", \"Result Unit\")\n\n  prep \u003c- function(type, suffix) {\n    out \u003c- dat[dat[[\"Activity Type\"]] == type, c(key, \"Result Value\",\n                                                 \"Result Detection Limit Value 1\")]\n    out[[\"Result Value\"]] \u003c- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(out[[\"Result Value\"]]))\n    out[[\"Result Detection Limit Value 1\"]] \u003c-\n      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(out[[\"Result Detection Limit Value 1\"]]))\n    out \u003c- out[!duplicated(out[key]), ]\n    names(out)[names(out) == \"Result Value\"] \u003c- paste0(\"result_\", suffix)\n    names(out)[names(out) == \"Result Detection Limit Value 1\"] \u003c- paste0(\"loq_\", suffix)\n    out\n  }\n\n  pairs \u003c- merge(prep(original_type, \"orig\"), prep(replicate_type, \"rep\"),\n                 by = key, all = FALSE)\n  names(pairs)[seq_along(key)] \u003c-\n    c(\"monitoring_location_id\", \"activity_start_date\", \"characteristic_name\",\n      \"sample_fraction\", \"method_id\", \"unit\")\n\n  pairs$loq \u003c- pmax(pairs$loq_orig, pairs$loq_rep, na.rm = TRUE)\n  pairs$loq[is.infinite(pairs$loq)] \u003c- NA_real_\n  pairs$rpd_pct \u003c- abs(pairs$result_orig - pairs$result_rep) /\n    ((pairs$result_orig + pairs$result_rep) / 2) * 100\n  pairs$threshold \u003c- ifelse(grepl(\"Nitrate|Nitrite|Phosphorus\", pairs$characteristic_name,\n                                  ignore.case = TRUE), 25,\n                     ifelse(grepl(\"suspended|solids\", pairs$characteristic_name,\n                                  ignore.case = TRUE), 5, 20))\n\n  lo \u003c- pmin(pairs$result_orig, pairs$result_rep)\n  hi \u003c- pairs$result_orig |> pmax(pairs$result_rep)\n  usable \u003c- !is.na(lo) & !is.na(pairs$loq)\n  rpd_ok \u003c- !is.na(pairs$rpd_pct) & is.finite(pairs$rpd_pct)\n  judge \u003c- ifelse(rpd_ok & pairs$rpd_pct \u003c= pairs$threshold, \"Pass\", \"Fail\")\n\n  # QAPP v3\n  q_elig \u003c- usable & hi > pairs$loq & hi >= 2 * pairs$loq\n  pairs$qapp_v3 \u003c- ifelse(q_elig & rpd_ok, judge, \"Not evaluable\")\n\n  # ADEC 2026\n  both_ge \u003c- usable & lo >= pairs$loq\n  one_below \u003c- usable & lo \u003c pairs$loq\n  pairs$adec_2026 \u003c- ifelse(both_ge & rpd_ok, judge,\n                     ifelse(one_below & hi >= 2 * pairs$loq, \"Fail\", \"Not evaluable\"))\n\n  pairs$rules_agree \u003c- pairs$qapp_v3 == pairs$adec_2026\n  pairs[order(pairs$monitoring_location_id, pairs$activity_start_date,\n              pairs$characteristic_name), ]\n}\n"},"elapsedMs":9}</script>

character(), rejected = logical())\n\n  # Batch and blank scopes\n  qb \u003c- f |> filter(scope %in% c(\"batch\", \"blank\")) |>\n    select(.qc_id, scope, lab_name, analytical_method, dissolved, q_analyte = analyte,\n           q_anl = anl_batch, q_prp = prp_batch, q_result = result, q_units = units,\n           sample_type, qc_check, batch_label)\n  m_batch \u003c- if (nrow(qb) == 0) empty else {\n    m \u003c- qb |>\n      inner_join(d, by = c(\"lab_name\", \"analytical_method\", \"dissolved\"),\n                 relationship = \"many-to-many\") |>\n      filter(batch_ok(q_anl, s_anl, q_prp, s_prp),\n             grepl(surr_pat, q_analyte, ignore.case = TRUE) | q_analyte == analyte)\n    is_blank \u003c- m$scope == \"blank\"\n    detected \u003c- !is.na(m$result) & !m$resultflag %in% c(\"U\", \"ND\")\n    if (any(is_blank & detected & !is.na(m$q_units) & !is.na(m$units) & m$q_units != m$units)) {\n      stop(\"assign_qc_status: a failing blank and the sample results it covers have different units\",\n           call. = FALSE)\n    }\n    m |> mutate(\n      rejected = !is_blank | (detected & !is.na(q_result) & result \u003c blank_multiple * q_result),\n      reason = \"parent\") |>\n    select(.qc_id, lab_name, analytical_method, dissolved, q_analyte = analyte, parent,\n           sample_type, qc_check)\n  m_parent \u003c- if (nrow(qp) == 0) empty else {\n    qp |>\n      inner_join(d, by = c(\"lab_name\", \"analytical_method\", \"dissolved\"),\n                 relationship = \"many-to-many\") |>\n      filter(!is.na(parent), lab_sample == parent, analyte == q_analyte) |>\n      mutate(rejected = TRUE,\n             reason = sprintf(\"Lab QC fail (%s %s on this sample)\", sample_type, qc_check)) |>\n      select(.qc_id, .row, reason, rejected)\n  }\n\n  # Sample scope (surrogates on field samples)\n  qs \u003c- f |> filter(scope == \"sample\") |>\n    select(.qc_id, lab_name, analytical_method, lab_sample_id, sample_type, qc_check)\n  m_sample \u003c- if (nrow(qs) == 0) empty else {\n    qs |>\n      inner_join(d, by = c(\"lab_name\", \"analytical_method\"), relationship = \"many-to-many\") |>\n      filter(!is.na(lab_sample_id), lab_sample == lab_sample_id) |>\n      mutate(rejected = TRUE,\n             reason = sprintf(\"Lab QC fail (surrogate %s on this sample)\", qc_check)) |>\n      select(.qc_id, .row, reason, rejected)\n  }\n\n  m_all \u003c- bind_rows(m_batch, m_parent, m_sample)\n\n  by_row \u003c- m_all |>\n    filter(rejected) |>\n    group_by(.row) |>\n    summarise(qc_fail_reason = paste(unique(reason), collapse = \"; \"), .groups = \"drop\")\n\n  out \u003c- dat |>\n    mutate(.row = row_number()) |>\n    left_join(by_row, by = \".row\") |>\n    mutate(qc_status = if_else(is.na(qc_fail_reason), \"Accepted\", \"Rejected\")) |>\n    select(-.row)\n\n  counts \u003c- m_all |>\n    group_by(.qc_id) |>\n    summarise(n_matched = n(), n_rejected = sum(rejected), .groups = \"drop\")\n  actions \u003c- f |>\n    left_join(counts, by = \".qc_id\") |>\n    mutate(n_matched = coalesce(n_matched, 0L), n_rejected = coalesce(n_rejected, 0L)) |>\n    select(sample_type, qc_group, qc_check, analyte, analytical_method, sample_id, anl_batch,\n           prp_batch, scope, n_matched, n_rejected)\n\n  list(dat = out, lab_qc_actions = actions)\n}\n","language":"r"}}</script>

The MS/MSD parent check came out fine, so option B is implemented. [functions/assign_qc_status.R](functions/assign_qc_status.R) and the batch table are in. All 13 test files pass, and the new one has 13 test blocks.

**Parent sample ID.** Every MS/MSD row has one, in the leading digits of its `sample_id`: - **Our samples (14 rows).** Rows like `1251731006MS` have a parent that matches a sample in `dat`. - **Other clients' samples (18 rows).** Rows like `1251737001 MS FOR [WFI3187]` have a parent that isn't ours. These reject nothing and are listed in `lab_qc_actions` with `n_matched` 0.

**What changed** - **`sample_batches`:** SGS batch IDs come from the EDD. Fecal coliform and TSS get a synthetic batch per lab, method and season (for example `SWWTP-2540-D-spring`), also written to their `lab_qc` rows. `combine_dat()` now returns the table, and the 25-column `dat` contract is untouched. - **`assign_qc_status()` rules:** - **Batch-wide:** LCS, LCSD, CCV, ICV, CVC, QCS, LLQC and surrogates on control samples reject every same-batch result for that analyte and method. - **Blanks:** a failing blank rejects detected results below 5× the blank result. A unit mismatch stops the run. - **MS/MSD:** a failure rejects only the parent sample. - **Surrogates on field samples:** a failure rejects that sample's results for the method. - **Outputs:** the function returns `dat` plus `qc_status` and `qc_fail_reason`, and a `lab_qc_actions` table for Q20. - **2025 fixture:** 49 of 857 results are Rejected (nitrate/nitrite, zinc and TSS). All come from blank rules or MS/MSD parents. No batch-control QC row failed. - **Notes:** `known_issues.md` and `pending_tasks.md` are updated. The "MS/MSD batch-wide" decision there is marked superseded.

**Not done yet** - **Q19 failures:** `assess_rpd()` works on the WQX-formatted export columns, not `dat`. To apply its failures, `format_wqx.R` needs to carry a `dat` row key through. - **Manual decisions and export:** the manual decisions file is not folded in. `generate_cdx_export.R` still maps the old Y/N flag, so Result Status ID, the `QCF` qualifier and Result Comment are not wired to `qc_status`. All of this depends on the row key. - **Reason text:** it can get long, because one reason is written per matching blank row. I'd shorten it before the export.

<script type="application/json">{"version":2,"name":"write","input":{"file_path":"functions/finalize_qc_status.R","content":"# finalize_qc_status.R\n#\n# Adds the two QC sources that can only be applied to the WQX-for...[truncated, total 4326 chars]"},"caption":"functions/finalize_qc_status.R","captionLink":"functions/finalize_qc_status.R","inputPreview":{"type":"code","value":"# finalize_qc_status.R\n#\n# Adds the two QC sources that can only be applied to the WQX-formatted export to the\n# lab-QC status that assign_qc_status() already carried through format_wqx.R:\n#   1. Q19 field duplicate failures (assess_rpd(), QAPP v3 rule): both the original and\n#      the replicate result are Rejected.\n#   2. The manual decisions file (rows with flag \"Y\"), matched on monitoring location,\n#      activity start date and characteristic name.\n# A result is Rejected if any source rejects it; reasons are joined with \"; \".\n#\n# Arguments\n#   export_dat    the intermediate export with snake_case names (janitor::clean_names()), including\n#                 qc_status, qc_fail_reason, activity_type, monitoring_location_id,\n#                 activity_start_date, characteristic_name, result_sample_fraction,\n#                 result_analytical_method_id, result_unit\n#   rpd_pairs     assess_rpd() output, or NULL\n#   manual_flags  data frame with monitoring_location_id, activity_start_date, characteristic_name,\n#                 flag, notes (optional column), or NULL. Unmatched \"Y\" rows give a warning.\n# Returns export_dat with qc_status, qc_fail_reason and flag (\"Y\" when Rejected, else \"N\").\n\nfinalize_qc_status \u003c- function(export_dat, rpd_pairs = NULL, manual_flags = NULL,\n                               original_type = \"Field Msr/Obs\",\n                               replicate_type = \"Quality Control Field Replicate Msr/Obs\") {\n  need \u003c- c(\"qc_status\", \"qc_fail_reason\", \"activity_type\", \"monitoring_location_id\",\n            \"activity_start_date\", \"characteristic_name\", \"result_sample_fraction\",\n            \"result_analytical_method_id\", \"result_unit\")\n  miss \u003c- setdiff(need, names(export_dat))\n  if (length(miss) > 0) {\n    stop(\"finalize_qc_status: export_dat is missing column(s): \", paste(miss, collapse = \", \"),\n         call. = FALSE)\n  }\n\n  d \u003c- export_dat\n  key \u003c- function(...) paste(..., sep = \"|\")\n  add_reason \u003c- function(existing, idx, text) {\n    existing[idx] \u003c- ifelse(is.na(existing[idx]), text, paste(existing[idx], text, sep = \"; \"))\n    existing\n  }\n  reason \u003c- d$qc_fail_reason\n  reason[!is.na(reason) & reason == \"\"] \u003c- NA_character_\n  rejected \u003c- d$qc_status %in% \"Rejected\"\n\n  # Q19: both rows of a failing pair\n  if (!is.null(rpd_pairs) && nrow(rpd_pairs) > 0) {\n    fails \u003c- rpd_pairs[rpd_pairs$qapp_v3 %in% \"Fail\", , drop = FALSE]\n    if (nrow(fails) > 0) {\n      pk \u003c- key(fails$monitoring_location_id, as.character(fails$activity_start_date),\n                fails$characteristic_name, fails$sample_fraction, fails$method_id, fails$unit)\n      ek \u003c- key(d$monitoring_location_id, as.character(d$activity_start_date),\n                d$characteristic_name, d$result_sample_fraction, d$result_analytical_method_id,\n                d$result_unit)\n      hit \u003c- match(ek, pk)\n      idx \u003c- which(d$activity_type %in% c(original_type, replicate_type) & !is.na(hit))\n      reason \u003c- add_reason(reason, idx,\n        sprintf(\"Field duplicate RPD fail (QAPP v3): %.1f%% exceeds %g%%\",\n                fails$rpd_pct[hit[idx]], fails$threshold[hit[idx]]))\n      rejected[idx] \u003c- TRUE\n    }\n  }\n\n  # Manual decisions\n  if (!is.null(manual_flags) && nrow(manual_flags) > 0) {\n    mf \u003c- manual_flags[manual_flags$flag %in% \"Y\", , drop = FALSE]\n    if (nrow(mf) > 0) {\n      notes \u003c- if (\"notes\" %in% names(mf)) mf$notes else rep(NA_character_, nrow(mf))\n      mk \u003c- key(mf$monitoring_location_id, as.character(as.Date(mf$activity_start_date)),\n                mf$characteristic_name)\n      ek \u003c- key(d$monitoring_location_id, as.character(as.Date(d$activity_start_date)),\n                d$characteristic_name)\n      unmatched \u003c- !mk %in% ek\n      if (any(unmatched)) {\n        warning(\"finalize_qc_status: manual flag row(s) matched no result: \",\n                paste(mk[unmatched], collapse = \"; \"), call. = FALSE)\n      }\n      text \u003c- ifelse(is.na(notes) | notes == \"\", \"Manual flag\",\n                     paste0(\"Manual flag: \", notes))\n      for (i in seq_along(mk)) {\n        idx \u003c- which(ek == mk[i])\n        if (length(idx) > 0) {\n          reason \u003c- add_reason(reason, idx, text[i])\n          rejected[idx] \u003c- TRUE\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  d$qc_fail_reason \u003c- reason\n  d$qc_status \u003c- ifelse(rejected, \"Rejected\", \"Accepted\")\n  d$flag \u003c- ifelse(rejected, \"Y\", \"N\")\n  d\n}\n","language":"r"}}</script>

    - **Required columns:** the function now needs `loq` and `dl`, not `repdl`.
    - **Output columns:** `blank_qapp` and `blank_adec` (NA on non-blank rows).
    - **QAPP rule (primary, drives `qc_result`):** a blank fails on any detection (flag not `U`/`ND`; if the flag is missing, a result above `dl`).
    - **ADEC rule (comparison only):** a blank fails at or above `loq`.
    - **2025 fixture:** 12 of 329 blank rows fail QAPP, and 1 of those also fails ADEC.
2.  **Blank multiple decided as 5x.**
    - **Config:** `config.yml` has `qc: blank_multiple: 5` (inserted via R, preserving line endings).
    - **Draft Q20 text:** it is stored in `topics/known_issues.md`. It says the QAPP is silent, 5x is a KWF project convention, ADEC's rule is shown beside it for comparison, and Rejected results stay public.
    - **Basis for choosing 5x over 10x:** fewer rejected results (about 91 vs 124 on a batch proxy), at the cost of a weaker contamination guard. No published source was found for either multiple.
3.  **`sample_batches` side table.**
    - **SGS (`ingest_sgs.R`):** it takes `anl_batch` and `prp_batch` from the EDD.
    - **FC and TSS (`ingest_fc.R`, `ingest_tss.R`):** synthetic batch ID `<lab>-<method>-<season>`, also written to their `lab_qc$anl_batch`.
    - **Return:** each ingest returns `sample_batches`, and `combine_dat()` returns it. `combine_dat.R` was rewritten wholesale (LF) after a blank-line mishap. The 25-column `dat` contract is unchanged.
4.  **`assign_qc_status()` (`functions/assign_qc_status.R`, `tests/test_assign_qc_status.R`; 13 test blocks pass).** Option B was chosen by the user.
    - **Batch-wide scope:** LCS, LCSD, CCV, ICV, CVC, QCS, LLQC and surrogates on control samples reject every same-batch, same-analyte, same-method result. Surrogate analytes match on method only.
    - **Blank scope:** a failing blank rejects detected results below `blank_multiple` × the blank result, in the same batch. The function stops if units differ.
    - **MS/MSD scope:** a failure rejects only the parent sample. The parent lab sample ID is the leading digits of the MS `sample_id`. Rows like "N MS FOR \[batch\]" are another client's sample and match nothing.
    - **Surrogates on field samples:** a failure rejects that sample's results for the method.
    - **Batch link:** equal `anl_batch` or equal `prp_batch`.
    - **Returns:** `list(dat, lab_qc_actions)`, where `dat` has `qc_status` (Accepted/Rejected) and `qc_fail_reason`, and `lab_qc_actions` has scope, `n_matched` and `n_rejected` per failing QC row, for Q20.
    - **Decision change:** the earlier "MS/MSD batch-wide" decision is superseded. The reason is that only MS/MSD rows failed in 2025 (6 nitrate/nitrite rows, with LCS, CCV and ICV all passing), which points to matrix effects.
    - **2025 fixture:** 49 of 857 results Rejected from lab QC (nitrate/nitrite, zinc, TSS).
5.  **Export wiring.**
    - **`format_wqx.R` (CRLF):** it adds `dat_row` (stops if a lookup join duplicates rows) and carries `dat_row`, `qc_status` and `qc_fail_reason` into the intermediate CSV.
    - **`functions/finalize_qc_status.R` and `tests/test_finalize_qc_status.R` (new, 7 test blocks pass):**

      - Manual decision rows with flag `Y` reject matching rows (note becomes the reason). A manual row that matches nothing triggers a warning.
      - It adds a `flag` Y/N column.

That is already on the SGS question list.

| `status` | Accepted, Rejected, and what each means in this pipeline |

Yes, placeholders are there to keep the text year-agnostic. Here is the detail.

**The problem** A usability statement says what the data can and cannot be used for. Part of it is fixed policy: results are public, Rejected results stay in the dataset, `QCF` marks QC failures, the 5x blank multiple is a project convention. Part of it depends on the year: how many results were Rejected, which analytes were affected, which QC checks failed, and whether any batches were unlinked. If you type the second part by hand each year, it goes stale, or a 2025 number ends up in a 2026 report. That is the failure the template is meant to avoid.

**Three ways to handle it**

| Option | How it works | Trade-off |
|----|----|----|
| A. Fixed text only | The statement contains only policy, no numbers. The year-specific counts live in the Q20 and Q19 tables of `qaqc.qmd`, which the statement points to. | Simplest and safest. The statement can't be wrong, but it gives the reader no summary numbers. |
| B. Placeholders in a markdown file | `reference/usability_statement.md` holds the text with tokens like `{{n_rejected}}` and `{{pct_rejected}}`. A small function fills them from `assessed_results.csv` at render time. | One place to edit the wording. Needs a fill function and a check that every token is filled. |
| C. Inline R in `prelim_report.qmd` | The statement is written in the Quarto file with inline R (`` `r n_rejected` ``). | No extra function and no separate file. The wording sits in the report, so `qaqc.qmd` and any other consumer can't reuse it. |

**Recommendation:** A, with a short sentence of live numbers added later if you want it. The policy text is the same every year, and the year-specific facts already have a home in the QC tables. When you want summary numbers, C is the natural step, because `prelim_report.qmd` already reads `assessed_results.csv` and Phase D will have the counts in hand. B adds a template engine to maintain for what is about five sentences.

Under A, the statement would be `reference/usability_statement.md`. `prelim_report.qmd` would include it with a Quarto include, and it would contain no numbers.

Which do you want: A, B or C?

[Go with option A: fixed policy text in reference/usability_statement.md, no placeholders.]{.suggestion}

Each result carries a Result Status of either Accepted or Rejected.\n\nA result is Rejected when it fails one of three checks:\n\n- **Laboratory QC.** A failing laboratory control sample, calibration verification, surrogate or similar check rejects the results in the same analytical batch for the same analyte and method. A failing matrix spike or matrix spike duplicate rejects only its parent sample, because those failures reflect the sample matrix and not the batch.\n- **Blanks.** A laboratory blank with any detection rejects detected results in the same batch that are below a set multiple of the blank result. The multiple is a Kenai Watershed Forum project convention, stated in `config.yml`. The QAPP does not specify one.\n- **Field duplicates.** A duplicate pair that fails the relative percent difference criterion in the QAPP rejects both results of the pair.\n\nRejected results are flagged with the qualifier `QCF` in Result Qualifier, and the reason is recorded in Result Comment. Rejected results are not removed from the dataset. Users who need only data that passed QA/QC should filter on Result Status.\n\nField blank and trip blank results are reported and listed in the blank check of the QA/QC report. They do not currently cause other results to be Rejected.\n\nLow level quantitation check (LLQC) samples are not evaluated, because acceptance limits are not documented. Qualifier codes follow QAPP v3 Table 7; definitions are in `reference/qualifier_definitions.csv`. Counts of Rejected results, the analytes affected and the checks that failed are given in the QA/QC report for the year.\n","language":"markdown"}}</script>

The QAPP's primary goal falls inside ADEC's range, but the secondary goal does not.

|   | Formula | Goal | Basis |
|----|----|----|----|
| QAPP v3 measure 1 (primary) | collected ÷ usable (as worded) | 85% | per analyte, site and overall |
| QAPP v3 measure 2 (secondary) | planned ÷ usable (as worded) | 60% | same |
| QAPP v3 formula | $$100\% \times (T - (I + NC)) / T$$ with T expected, I invalid, NC not produced or rejected | none stated |  |
| ADEC 2026 guidance | same formula, I includes not collected, rejected, spilled | 80-90% | each analytical parameter and field measurement type |

**Findings** - **Wording and formula disagree.** As worded, both QAPP measures are inverted. "Collected ÷ usable" and "planned ÷ usable" would exceed 100% whenever anything is lost. The QAPP's own formula, and the legacy `2023.qmd`, use usable ÷ collected for A and usable ÷ planned for B. - **The reading is consistent.** Collected is at most planned, so B is never higher than A. That fits B having the lower goal (60%). - **The 85% goal is within ADEC's 80-90%.** The 60% secondary goal is below ADEC's range. ADEC's formula (T is expected, and not-collected counts as invalid) is numerically the QAPP's B, so ADEC's 80-90% would be compared against B. I'd show the QAPP goals as primary and ADEC's range beside them, as for Q19. - **Required output.** The QAPP's reporting section asks for a completeness table per analyte: scheduled, collected and valid, and the required goal. Both measures are also stated for individual sites. - **Legacy code has three problems.** - It treats "usable" as the manual flag `N`. It should now be `qc_status == "Accepted"`. - Q26 uses the actual counts as the planned counts in 2025, so B is circular. No planned-sample file exists. - Counts mix QC sample types.

**Question 1 of a few:** may I use these definitions? - A = Accepted results ÷ results collected (all non-QC primary results that exist in `dat`). - B = Accepted results ÷ planned results.

The planned count would come from a template-supplied design file, which is the harder part. I'll ask about that after your answer.

## Working preferences

- Explain code before writing and wait for confirmation. Present decisions one at a time. Approval of a design is the go-ahead to write it.
- No em-dashes; minimal AI-writing tropes. Do not interpret trends in text.
- Never record or code 2025-specific counts as expectations; label them test-fixture results.
- Never modify originals; write `_corrected`, `_v2` or `_reconciled` copies beside them.
- All ingest scripts emit `mg/L`. Never include the `KENAI_WQX-` prefix in any ID column.
- **Line endings:** `AGENTS.md`, `format_wqx.R`, `ingest_*.R`, `check_dat_contract.R`, `check_cdx_ids.R`, `extract_ars_pdf.R`, `reference/dat_contract.md`, `tests/test_combine_dat.R` and `functions/assess_lab_qc.R` are CRLF. `generate_cdx_export.R` has doubled CRs (CR CR LF) that exist in git. `combine_dat.R`, `apply_qaqc_flags.R`, `assess_rpd.R`, `assign_qc_status.R`, `finalize_qc_status.R` and most tests are LF.
- **Editing CRLF files:** the edit tool fails on multi-line matches. Edit through R with a byte-level helper (`readBin`, `fixed` `sub`, `writeBin`). Or read with `sub("\r+$", "", ...)` and write with `con <- file(f, "wb"); writeLines(l, con, sep = "\r\n")`. Check for doubled CRs afterwards.
- **Tests:** use testthat with `reporter = "silent"` and `as.data.frame(results)`. Save results to a variable and print it in a separate call.
- **Shell and temp paths:** do not run a bash heredoc that invokes `python3`; it hung the shell once. Writes to the OS temp directory from the R session can be blocked, so use paths inside the repo and clean up afterwards.
